content:
The design system spec holds records: components, patterns, guidelines, and examples. A component
is a technology-neutral contract (anatomy, parameters, states, rules, tokens), not framework code.
Implement it in whatever technology the project uses.

- Use the `taproot` CLI when you have a terminal, and the `taproot` MCP server when you
  do not. Run the CLI from an installed copy, never an `npx` download per call: in this repository,
  `node packages/spec/bin/taproot.js`; in a project that depends on the package,
  `node_modules/.bin/taproot`.
- Start with `search` to choose a component, then `get` it and follow its links: `alternative` for
  when it is the wrong choice, `follows` for the patterns and guidelines it applies, `examples` for
  worked usage.
- Use `rules` to review work, and cite each rule by its address (for example
  `component.button#label-describes-result`) with its level (MUST, SHOULD, MAY).
- Use `tokens` for the design tokens a component part uses in a variant or state. Add `--resolve`
  (MCP: `resolve`) for values. Use `format` for what records do not repeat: the system-wide
  constants, such as border width and focus-ring width and offset, with their tokens.
- Before writing code, `get` the component with the implementation for your technology:
  `--impl web` for web components, `--impl react` for React (MCP: `implementation`). It gives the
  package, what to import, and the attribute or prop that implements each parameter. Never derive
  those names from parameter names.
- For several lookups, run them in one `batch` with the CLI (for example
  `taproot batch --command "get button --impl web" --command "tokens button"`), or make the
  tool calls in parallel on the MCP server.

Exit code 1
$ taproot list
- component.accordion — Accordion: Use Accordion to let people expand only the sections of a long page they need, one heading at a time.
- component.alert — Alert: Use Alert for a short status message in the flow of the page, announced only when you ask.
- component.avatar — Avatar: Use Avatar to show a small picture of a person, so people can recognize who did, owns, or wrote something.
- component.badge — Badge: Use Badge for status or metadata. It is not a control.
- component.button — Button: Use Button to trigger an action or to submit or reset a form.
- component.card — Card: Use Card to present one subject as a bounded summary, such as an item in a collection, that a person can scan and act on.
- component.checkbox — Checkbox: Use Checkbox to turn one independent option on or off, with a label, hint, and error.
- component.dialog — Dialog: Use Dialog for a focused task or confirmation that temporarily blocks the surrounding view.
- component.divider — Divider: Use Divider to separate groups of related content within one surface or region with a thin line.
- component.icon — Icon: Use Icon to size and color a graphic you supply, beside text or inside another component.
- component.link — Link: Use Link to navigate to another page, a location on the page, or a resource.
- component.progress-bar — Progress bar: Use Progress bar to show how much of a task is done when you can measure it, such as an upload or a multi-step setup.
- component.radio-group — Radio group: Use Radio group to choose exactly one option from a short visible list.
- component.select — Select: Use Select to choose one value from a list with a label, hint, and error.
- component.slider — Slider: Use Slider to choose one number from a continuous range when the approximate value matters more than the exact one.
- component.spinner — Spinner: Use Spinner to show that something is loading or working when you cannot say how long it will take.
- component.switch — Switch: Use Switch to turn a setting on or off and apply the change immediately.
- component.tabs — Tabs: Use Tabs to switch between a few related views of the same subject, one view visible at a time.
- component.text-area — Text area: Use Text area to collect multiple lines of text with a label, hint, and error.
- component.text-field — Text field: Use Text field to collect a single line of text with a label, hint, and error.
- component.tooltip — Tooltip: Use Tooltip to show the name of an icon-only control when a person points at it or focuses it.
- example.action-hierarchy.settings — Settings action hierarchy: A settings screen separates routine profile actions from destructive account deletion.
- guideline.compose-or-propose — Compose or propose: Compose a new interface need from tokens and existing components first, and open an issue or RFC only when the system itself has to change.
- pattern.action-hierarchy — Action hierarchy: Assign action emphasis by importance, support role, and risk, and choose Button or Link by what the control does.
- pattern.form-field — Form field: Give every form control the same label, hint, error, required, disabled, and form behavior.

$ taproot get guideline.compose-or-propose
# Compose or propose

Compose a new interface need from tokens and existing components first, and open an issue or RFC only when the system itself has to change.

Most interface needs are met by composing what the system already publishes. Change the system
only when composition cannot express the need without copying or overriding a component.

## Compose first

Work through these in order and stop at the first one that meets the need:

1. A published variant, size, or parameter of an existing component.
2. Existing components placed together in product markup, such as a Badge beside a Button or a
   Link after an action group.
3. Product layout and chrome styled with semantic tokens. Use a primitive token only when no
   semantic role expresses the choice.

A composition that meets the need stays in product code. It does not need an issue, a record, or
a review.

## Do not fork a component

Composition stops being composition when product code rebuilds what a component owns. Do not:

- Copy a component's styles or structure to make a variant that the contract does not publish.
- Restyle a component's internal parts, or override the tokens it reads, to create a variant,
  state, or size the contract does not publish.
- Define component tokens in product code.
- Use one component to do another's job, such as a Badge as a control or a Link styled as a
  Button. The action hierarchy pattern says which control fits which job.
- Rebuild a component's states, focus ring, or accessible name handling in a new element.

When one of these is the only way to meet the need, the system is missing something. Propose it.

## Propose a change

Open an issue on the design system when the change fits the components and tokens it already has:

- A variant, size, or parameter on an existing component.
- A bug in a component, one of its implementations, a token, or its documentation.
- A composition used in more than one place that should become a pattern.
- A new component whose behavior comes from a standard platform control plus tokens, such as an
  icon or a field shell.

Some changes alter how the system works, not only what it contains. Say so in the issue, so the
design question is settled before anyone writes code:

- A component that owns focus management, an overlay, or a composite keyboard model, such as a
  Dialog, Select, Menu, or Tabs.
- A new token tier, or a semantic role category that does not exist yet.

$ taproot get component.text-field
# Text field

Use Text field to collect a single line of text with a label, hint, and error.

Collects one line of text and associates a label, optional hint, and optional error with the control.

## When to use

- Collect a short value such as a name, email, or search query.
- Pair with Button when the value should be submitted.

## When not to use

- Collect multi-line text. Use [Text area](component.text-area) instead. Text field is a single line.
- Choose from a known set of options. Use [Select](component.select) instead. Text field does not present choices.
- Trigger an action by itself. Use [Button](component.button) instead. Text field collects a value.

## Anatomy

| Part | Role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| field | container | Label, control, hint, and error stacked together. |
| label | label | Visible name for the value. |
| control | interactive-surface | Single-line text control. |
| hint | description | Optional supporting guidance. |
| error | description | Optional message that says what to fix. |

## Parameters

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | string |  |  | Visible label. This is the accessible name. |
| hint | string |  |  | Supporting guidance. Included in the accessible description when set. |
| error | string |  |  | What to fix. A non-empty value marks the control invalid and is included in the accessible description. |
| type | enum | `text`, `email`, `password`, `search`, `url`, `tel` | `text` |  |
| name | string |  |  | Form field name. The value is submitted under this name. |
| value | string |  |  | Current value. The value given at creation is the initial value that reset restores. |
| placeholder | string |  |  | Example text shown when the value is empty. Not a replacement for the label. |
| autocomplete | string |  |  | Guidance for automatic filling from previously supplied information, such as email. |
| disabled | boolean |  | `false` | Prevents editing. A disabled field does not submit its value. |
| required | boolean |  | `false` | The value must be provided before submit. Conveyed by more than color. |

`type` values:

- `text`: Plain single-line text.
- `email`: Email address.
- `password`: Concealed secret.
- `search`: Search query.
- `url`: Web address.
- `tel`: Telephone number.

## Events

- `input`: The value changed while editing.
- `change`: The value was committed.

## States

`disabled`, `invalid`, `hover`, `focus`, `default`

## Accessibility

- Role: Text input
- Name: Required from the visible label.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Move focus to or from the field. |
| Printable characters | Insert text. |

## Rationale

- **Text field consumes semantic tokens directly.** Tokens ADR 0003. Focus, invalid, disabled, surface, and text already have semantic roles. No component-token namespace.
- **Invalid is a state driven by the error message.** The message is the accessible signal. A variant axis would hide that the state comes from the error.
- **Label, hint, and error belong to the field.** A separate field shell does not exist yet. Association stays on this control until that shell lands.

## Links

### alternative

- [Button](component.button) — Trigger an action by itself. Text field collects a value.
- [Select](component.select) — Choose from a known set of options. Text field does not present choices.
- [Text area](component.text-area) — Collect multi-line text. Text field is a single line.

### alternative-to

- [Slider](component.slider) — Enter an exact number, or a number from a very large range. Typing is faster and more precise than dragging to one value among hundreds.
- [Text area](component.text-area) — Collect a short single-line value. Text field keeps short values compact.
- [Tooltip](component.tooltip) — Explain the expected format of a form field, or why its value is invalid. The field's hint and error are always visible and are read with the field. A tooltip hides the information until someone goes looking for it.

### follows

- [Compose or propose](guideline.compose-or-propose)
- [Form field](pattern.form-field)

### related

- [Badge](component.badge)
- [Checkbox](component.checkbox)
- [Select](component.select)
- [Slider](component.slider)
- [Text area](component.text-area)

$ taproot get component.popover
Unknown record "component.popover".

**Taproot doesn't have a date picker or calendar popup component.** I searched for one and checked the full component list. The closest fit, Text field, doesn't support dates either: its `type` values are `text`, `email`, `password`, `search`, `url` and `tel`.

`guideline.compose-or-propose` leaves you two realistic options:

- **Available now (my recommendation): typed date entry.** Use Text field, with the expected format in `hint` (for example, "YYYY-MM-DD") and validation problems in `error`. It's the only option that stays within the published components, but there's no calendar popup. Text field's only implementation is for web components, so a React project would have to implement the contract itself.
- **If you need the calendar: propose it to the design system.** Open an issue, and say that this changes how the system works, because a calendar popup owns focus management, an overlay and a composite keyboard model. The design question then gets settled before anyone writes code.

Don't build the popup by restyling Dialog or copying Text field's internals, as the guideline counts that as forking a component. Dialog is also meant for a focused task that blocks the surrounding view, which is heavy for picking a date.

If the booking form can only offer a few dates, such as available slots, Select or Radio group would also work without a calendar.
